name: net force
definition: All the forces on an object added together, taking their directions into account. If they cancel, the net force is zero and the motion does not change.

name: force
definition: A push or a pull. Every force has a size and a direction, and it can start, stop, speed up, slow down or turn a motion.

name: friction
definition: A force that acts against sliding wherever two surfaces rub together. It is what slows a sliding book or a rolling ball.

name: inertia
definition: An object's resistance to any change in its motion. The more mass something has, the more inertia it has.

name: velocity
definition: Speed together with a direction. Turning at a steady speed still changes the velocity.

name: mass
definition: How much matter an object has. It tells you how hard the object is to speed up or slow down.

name: acceleration
definition: How much the velocity changes every second. Speeding up, slowing down and turning are all acceleration.

name: newton
definition: The unit of force. One newton speeds up 1 kg by 1 m/s every second, about the weight of a small apple.

name: force pair
definition: The two forces two objects put on each other. They are equal in size, opposite in direction, and act on different objects.

name: momentum
definition: Mass times velocity. When objects push on each other, their total momentum stays the same.
